rubric: Derive the contract from the public request, explicit issue-time owner decisions, and relevant pre-change behavior. Require each criterion to state a supported, externally observable outcome or compatibility boundary. Treat internal mechanisms, code structure, predicates, data representations, control flow, exact messages, documentation edits, refactors, and test construction or placement as optional unless a source explicitly makes them observable requirements. Use later patches, diagnoses, and tests only to clarify the defect, demonstrate a directly relevant outcome, or confirm non-regression; do not let them retroactively require the reference implementation, incidental fixture details, broader input coverage, or hindsight-only choices. Include material owner-resolved boundaries, reject unresolved or unsupported additions, penalize scope expansion and compatibility regressions, and accept any implementation that satisfies the supported observable contract.
